basis: Defined CNS, renal and soft-tissue origins; hepatic tumors occur in 30-79% per supplied HPO. Additional reported sites omitted under the four-axis cap.
Benign tumor arising in the iris.
Congenital multiple joint contractures and deafness define the syndrome; inguinal hernias do not establish intrinsic intestinal damage.
Defining limb and vertebral malformations; duodenal atresia in 80-99% and thymic aplasia in 30-79% support intestinal and immune involvement.
Endocrine dysfunction, neurodevelopmental/movement disorder and alopecia define it; hearing loss in 4/7 and HPO 80-99%. Frequent osteopenia omitted under cap.
Exercise-triggered bronchial narrowing defines this airway disorder; no additional organ damage is established.
Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the exocrine pancreas; secondary diabetes is a separate diagnosis.
Defining skeletal malformations; cardiovascular abnormalities 80-99%, choanal atresia and renal anomalies 30-79%. Steroidogenesis defects are subtype-specific.
Defective respiratory ciliary clearance with bronchiectasis; recurrent middle-ear inflammation in 11/11 supports otologic involvement.
Collapsing glomerular injury causes steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome; an immune mechanism is not established by this designation.
Isolated skin and hair pigment disorder; this subtype lacks immunologic or neurologic disease, and iris hypopigmentation is occasional.
Combined immunodeficiency, pancytopenia and microcephaly/developmental impairment define it; hypothyroidism in 2/4. Photosensitivity alone does not establish skin damage.
Premature fusion of the coronal and metopic skull sutures; no syndromic organ involvement is established.
Immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis with defining cutaneous purpura; neuropathy and renal injury are not established at >=30% for type III.
Adenoid enlargement occupies the nasopharyngeal airway; associated otitis media is a separate condition.
Structural collapse of the foot's longitudinal arch.
Neuroblastoma in the neck arises from the cervical sympathetic nervous system.
Inherited platelet deficiency and dysfunction; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate skin or airway damage.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy and pituitary insufficiency define it; retinal dystrophy occurs in only 1/7, and nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; heart defects, unilateral renal agenesis and ophthalmological anomalies are explicitly described as common, although frequencies are unquantified.
Congenital shortening and webbing of digits constitute a skeletal developmental disorder.
Congenital mitral valve incompetence directly affects cardiac valve function.
Congenital absence of gluteal skeletal muscles.
Malignant T-cell precursors occupy blood and marrow; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly half or more. Thymic masses do not establish lung involvement.
Benign fibrous tumor confined to the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the specified axes.
